routes.description: Establish that evolutionary naturalism supplies defeaters for rational confidence in the cognitive faculties used to affirm naturalism, without requiring proof that a supernatural alternative is true.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalism's account of belief formation leaves no adequate warrant for trusting human cognition about ultimate reality and the objection cannot be answered merely by demanding evidence of the supernatural.

motionBridge.description: Show that a worldview which undermines warrant for the cognition affirming it cannot itself be rationally affirmed.

centralBridges.description: Establish that physical determination, randomness, or causally idle mental states do not by themselves make beliefs responsive to rational grounds or truth.
Establish that selection for survival and reproduction does not ensure reliable cognition when faculties are extended to comprehensive metaphysical conclusions.
Establish that naturalism may be rejected or rational confidence withheld because of internal incoherence without first demonstrating a supernatural realm.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish metaphysical naturalism from scientific method and require a positive defense of the claim that only nature exists.
Test whether naturalism permits any contrary observation to count against it rather than automatically receiving a natural reinterpretation.

routes.description: Defend rational confidence in naturalism through provisional reliance on cognition, evolved capacities for dependable interaction, and publicly testable evidence while assigning the supernatural claimant the burden of demonstrating an addition to the known natural world.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if objective inquiry supplies a workable basis for corrigible confidence in natural conclusions, the evolutionary reliability objection does not establish global defeat, and no verified supernatural exception displaces the natural account.

motionBridge.description: Show that naturalism remains rationally warranted by objective evidence unless its alleged self-defeat is established or a supernatural exception is demonstrated.

centralBridges.description: Account for sufficiently dependable cognition through unavoidable provisional reliance on experience, evolved social capacities, and correction by shared objective inquiry.
Challenge the asserted connections among naturalism, determinism, survival-directed evolution, and the conclusion that rational thought is unwarranted.
Require independent, repeatable, objective verification before adding supernatural entities or causes to the accepted natural world.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish evidence-governed methodological naturalism and acceptance of the known physical world from an unsupported universal negative about every immaterial possibility.
Specify observable conditions that could support supernatural claims and use repeated testing to preserve revisability rather than immunity from contrary evidence.

sections.title: Naturalism's Definition and Burden of Proof
sections.rationale: The dispute over whether naturalism asserts that only nature exists or provisionally accepts the known natural world determines what each side must establish and whether internal critique can resolve the motion.

sections.title: Physical Causation, Determinism, and Rational Agency
sections.rationale: The claimed gap between physical belief production and responsiveness to reasons is a major proposed mechanism of self-defeat, while objections concerning indeterminism, emergence, and rational processes test that inference.

sections.title: Evolutionary Fitness and Truth-Tracking Cognition
sections.rationale: Whether selection for survival can produce faculties reliable enough for abstract worldview judgments is the principal substantive clash identified by the motion and the central evolutionary component of both routes.

sections.title: Objective Evidence, Experience, and Cognitive Correction
sections.rationale: Appeals to testable data, provisional sensory trust, social cooperation, and collaborative checking bear directly on whether naturalism can justify corrigible confidence despite acknowledged cognitive limitations.

sections.title: Falsifiability and Evidence Beyond Nature
sections.rationale: Competing standards for miracles, prophecy, apparent design, and other purported supernatural effects test both naturalism's openness to disconfirmation and whether any alternative has met the proposed evidential threshold.
